selector.champion: Glioblastoma (World Health Organization grade IV) with optic nerve invasion and intraocular extension
selector.rationale: The presence of astrocytic neoplasm, positive for glial fibrillary acid protein, oligodendrocyte transcription factor 2, mutant IDH-1 protein, and loss of ATRX protein, along with the Ki-67 proliferation index, supports the diagnosis of a high-grade glioma, specifically Glioblastoma (World Health Organization grade IV) with optic nerve invasion and intraocular extension, given the optic disc swelling, peripapillary retinal hemorrhages, and vitreous biopsy results.

rejected.label: Central Retinal Artery Occlusion
rejected.why: While the patient developed central retinal artery occlusion, this appears to be a secondary complication rather than the primary diagnosis.

rejected.label: Astrocytic Neoplasm
rejected.why: This is a broader category that includes the champion diagnosis but is less specific.

rejected.label: Glioma
rejected.why: Less specific than the champion diagnosis, which provides more detail about the grade and extent of the tumor.

rejected.label: Glioblastoma
rejected.why: The champion diagnosis provides more specificity regarding the grade and invasion.

rejected.label: IDH-mutant Astrocytoma
rejected.why: The presence of mutant IDH-1 protein supports this, but the overall clinical and pathological picture better fits the champion diagnosis.
